question: Should OpenClaw expose a permanent trusted-plugin SDK capability that forwards an opaque run-scoped approval grant and permits requester-session completion routing into native harness execution?
rationale: This is not only a mechanical bug fix: it adds a security- and compatibility-sensitive plugin contract whose issuer, validation, expiry, revocation, and supported harness semantics determine the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow owned contract
options.body: Retain the capability after naming the approval-grant owner and validation contract, documenting the supported trusted-plugin use case, and adding real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep routing but defer approval passthrough
options.body: Land only requester completion routing if it is independently needed, and design approval handoff in a dedicated owner-reviewed protocol change.

options.title: Route the workflow outside core
options.body: Keep this behavior in the owner plugin until a shared core/native-harness API is demonstrably required.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow owned contract
recommendation.body: Retain the capability after naming the approval-grant owner and validation contract, documenting the supported trusted-plugin use case, and adding real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the Gateway trust boundary, plugin SDK compatibility contract, and native-harness execution semantics.
